paper: ContestTrade: A Multi-Agent Trading System Based on Internal Contest Mechanism
claim_boundary: A researcher-authored monthly U.S.-stock implementation of ContestTrade's dual Quantify-Predict-Allocate contests; not a native daily China A-share replication and not a test of the paper's reported 52.8% return or 3.12 Sharpe ratio.

primary_source_anchors.mechanism: A Data Team filters factor information in a first contest, then independent Research Agents compete in a second contest whose positive predicted-Sharpe weights form the final portfolio.
Both contests follow Quantify-Predict-Allocate: score delayed realized efficacy, forecast near-term utility from score history, and allocate scarce context or capital.
The Data Analyst Contest excludes negative-utility factors and uses a budgeted facility-location objective to retain valuable but non-redundant information.
The Researcher Contest combines realized performance with a bounded qualitative rubric, prevents judgment from overriding negative realized utility, and weights only positive predicted Sharpe ratios.
Only records and contest labels realized before portfolio formation may update later contest decisions.

contest_policy.data_quantification: monthly Spearman RankIC of each signed Data Agent score with next-month excess return
contest_policy.data_predicted_utility: 24-month mean RankIC plus one half of the difference between the most recent and preceding six-month means
contest_policy.data_similarity: absolute current cross-sectional correlation between Data Agent score ranks
contest_policy.data_allocation: lazy-equivalent deterministic greedy maximization of positive-utility facility-location coverage
contest_policy.data_no_positive_fallback: retain the single highest predicted-utility Data Agent so the fixed common path remains defined
contest_policy.research_predicted_utility: trailing mean Research Agent RankIC divided by its sample standard deviation
contest_policy.research_allocation: max(0, predicted Sharpe) times 0.90 plus 0.10 times the frozen judge score divided by five, normalized across agents
contest_policy.research_no_positive_fallback: allocate fully to the highest predicted-Sharpe Research Agent so the fixed common path remains defined
contest_policy.score_refresh: monthly; all contest outcomes come from formation months strictly before the current formation
contest_policy.common_portfolio_adapter: frozen value-weighted long-short deciles with the six cost and missing-return paths

preserved_elements: a first-stage contest that filters noisy factor information
a second-stage contest that allocates across independent research beliefs
the Quantify-Predict-Allocate sequence in both contests
delayed realized performance feedback rather than future labels at decision time
exclusion of negative predicted utility from normal allocation
budgeted facility-location selection for Data Agent value and diversity
momentum, reversal, fundamental, event-driven, and risk-control Research Agents
positive predicted-Sharpe weighting in the Researcher Contest
a bounded qualitative judgment complement that cannot rescue negative quantitative utility
approximated_elements: signed JKP characteristics replace LLM-generated textual factors
RankIC persistence replaces unreleased LightGBM factor-utility predictions
cross-sectional score correlation replaces text-embedding cosine similarity
deterministic factor sleeves replace LLM Plan-and-ReAct research traces
fixed rubric scores replace anonymous LLM judge-panel outputs
monthly U.S. stock updates replace five-day China A-share contest horizons
the common decile adapter replaces T+1, price-limit, and cash execution rules
invented_elements: the sixteen signed Data Agent definitions
the 24-month Data Contest history and six-month utility trend
the five exact Research Agent feature sleeves and judge scores
the equal 0.50 data-context and belief mixture
deterministic single-agent fallbacks when no predicted utility is positive
